chunks: 2381 - Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Muslim said:
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about Sindhi chickens being taken out of the Haram, and he said: “Yes, because they cannot fly independently.”
And in another report: “They only flutter lightly.”

key_terms.السِّنْدِيِّ: Sindhi; a specific type attributed to Sind
key_terms.تَدُفُّ: it flutters or moves its wings lightly
key_terms.تَسْتَقِلُّ: to be capable on its own; here, to fly independently

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take Sindhi chickens out of the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning Sindhi chickens in the Haram and permits taking them out. The reason given is that they are not considered independently flying birds, and another report clarifies that their movement is only a light fluttering.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2381 - Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Muslim reported that

Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about Sindhi chickens being taken out of the Haram.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, because they cannot fly independently."
In another narration: "They only flutter lightly."
